cards.front: What is a Direction Cosine Matrix (DCM) C?
cards.back: A 3×3 proper orthogonal matrix (C^T C = I, det(C)=1) whose rows/columns are the unit vectors of one frame expressed in the other; it rotates vector components via v_b = C v_i.

cards.front: Define the skew-symmetric cross-product matrix [ω×] for ω=[ω1,ω2,ω3]^T.
cards.back: $$[ω×]=\begin{bmatrix}0&-ω3&ω2\\ω3&0&-ω1\\-ω2&ω1&0\end{bmatrix}$$ so that [ω×]v=ω×v for any vector v.

cards.front: State the DCM kinematic equation Ċ=-[ω×]C.
cards.back: The first-order matrix ODE governing the time evolution of the attitude DCM C when the body angular velocity ω (expressed in the body frame) is known.

cards.front: Derive Ċ=-[ω×]C from the definition of C.
cards.back: Let ê_i be inertial basis vectors and ê_b(t) body basis vectors. Then C_{ij}=ê_b_i·ê_i_j. Differentiating and using ė_b_i=ω×ê_b_i yields Ċ=-[ω×]C after expressing the result in body coordinates.

cards.front: Prove that C(t) remains orthogonal for all t if Ċ=-[ω×]C and C(0)^T C(0)=I.
cards.back: d/dt(CC^T)=ĊC^T+CĊ^T=-[ω×]CC^T+C(-[ω×]C)^T. Because [ω×]^T=-[ω×], the right-hand side vanishes, so CC^T remains constant and equal to I.

cards.front: How is ω recovered from Ċ and C?
cards.back: $$[ω×]=-ĊC^T$$ (or equivalently ω=½(CĊ^T) where the vee operator extracts the vector from the skew-symmetric matrix).

cards.front: What happens to C(t) when ω(t)≡0?
In attitude propagation, why integrate Ċ=-[ω×]C rather than using Euler angles?
cards.back: The DCM equation is singularity-free, globally valid, and linear in C; Euler angles suffer from gimbal lock and nonlinear trigonometric kinematics.
